column1: # The units of the harness redo as tasks: ids and English briefs only. Load with
# One unit per line, five tab-separated columns:
# partOf is a label or '-'; blockedBy is a comma-separated list of labels. The task title is
# '<label> <name>', and a label that is already a task's first word is not created twice.

column5: The cap on unmerged work and the identity checks that keep agent pushes off the maintainer account.
Draft-first pull requests, series ids, present-check and the lander: how work reaches review and then main.
Tooling and cleanup that does not depend on the other lanes.

scripts/whoami-check prints the account git would push as, gh's active account and the SSH greeting; exit 0 always; nags when one of them is an admin and prints the token-URL push form; wired as a pre-push message; self-test under bash 3.2 and 5.

harness/rulesets/brake.json (all refs but main, creation and update, bypass for admins, the lander App and the deploy key, enforcement disabled), JSON exports of the live rulesets, and scripts/ruleset-check, a read-only drift check that exits 1 on drift.

scripts/wip-count (commits on open non-draft pull requests; prints N/50, M left) and a workflow draft that flips the brake ruleset on events and on a 15-minute schedule, idempotently, never checking out pull-request code; --dry-run; the lag goes to the job summary.

A staged patch for the local work-in-progress check: count commits on open pull requests, print the distance, never refuse; with sha256 and install and rollback lines; a replay over past commands gives 0 refusals. Staged only, never installed by an agent.
Complete the proof table on the scratch repository (rulesets, App permissions, dismissal behaviour) from forge reads: each row measured, or marked owner-only. Feeds A3 and A6a.

A --ci mode of scripts/land and a land workflow: workflow_dispatch with concurrency, a verify job without secrets and a land job in an environment with the lander App token; an approval on the exact head SHA is mandatory; writes the series check run, fast-forwards main, retargets children, deletes the head branch.
scripts/land --dry-run N prints every rule and the plain git sequence; every automated step is documented as a by-hand command; a range that touches workflows is routed to the owner path.

When an approved head is not an ancestor of main: cherry-pick it onto main in a verify job, require per-commit tree and pair equality in the land job, push main and then the head with a lease, post the old-to-new map. A differing pair goes to a candidate ref with a range-diff, never over the reviewed head.

scripts/pr bases on main by default (-B only for a real dependency on an open PR), opens as draft, and takes --body-file, --update-body and --ready through leak-check --text and the identity check; the FIFO and the pre-push gate-4 comment go; no labels.

Kernel-style topic-path branch names with no fixed leaf and no provenance; stack/ is legacy only; branch-lint, BRANCHES.md and every consumer (hooks, acommit, new-worktree, pr) follow, in three sub-series: grammar and lint, consumers, docs.

A Series-Id trailer after Stack in the trailer order, and scripts/series with mint, stamp, check, manifest (patch-id and message hash, digest, JSON), range and revert; commit-msg refuses two ids; series-self-test in make gates.

scripts/series present-check (tree equality, make quick per commit in a detached worktree, commit-lint, one Series-Id; prints the lemma list and range-diff) and a series workflow draft without secrets that labels pushes, posts the range-diff and relays an approving review as a land dispatch.

A presenter agent definition and an AGENTS.md pointer: a fresh session, never the builder, rewrites the work branch into the literate series, one lemma per commit, then the trailers, present-check, manifest and the review card through scripts/pr --update-body and --ready.
WORKFLOW.md, AGENTS.md, COMMITS.md, the CODEOWNERS comment and CLAUDE.md describe only what has landed (draft default, no FIFO, Series-Id, present-check, presenter, revert); stale claims removed.
The landing section: the App lands fast-forward, relocation, approve means land, the deploy-key owner path; no live mention of rebase-merge as a path.
The review page orders its queue by dependency instead of first in first out, and the approve-and-rebase-merge button becomes approve in the UI, with the lander landing it.
Remove scripts/mirror, import-pr, mirror-self-test, the pijul layer in flake.nix, the WORKFLOW.md mirror section and the in-repo references.
packages.oci in flake.nix (dockerTools.buildLayeredImage of the dev-shell closure), make image and a DEVSHELL.md note; make quick passes inside the container.
Shrink the maintainer's own agent-instruction file to a short core and give every rule a home elsewhere, with a table of where each paragraph went. Outside this repository.
Benchmark local models against the hosted one for the atomic-commit check on a labelled corpus of commits; report accuracy, latency and cost per model.
The atomic-check hook calls the chosen local model with the same {atomic, reason} contract, fails open with a loud warning, FPL_ATOMIC_STRICT=1 opts in to refusing, and keeps the verdict cache.
This list of units as scripts/task tasks (Radicle COBs, blockedBy and partOf), with task ready and task tree; every title and body goes through leak-check --text first.
The same DAG as a map issue with sub-issues and blocked-by relations on the scratch repository, with a gh one-liner that prints the tree.
Marker-based two-way sync between the Radicle store and the issue map, after both have been tried; a round trip leaves both stores equal.

scripts/sweep --dry-run lists every worktree and branch (merged, patch-new, dirty, PR state, owner, proposed action) with a do-not-touch list; --apply only on explicit maintainer approval, tags before removal.
Spec and pure-function tests for a sync-before-launch gate: a scope file (fixes, defers, never touches) acknowledged by its hash; a staged patch for the owner to install.
Every procedure lives in a skill under .agents/skills/ with its script; AGENTS.md is one screen of pointers; the docs keep decisions and rationale; a gate holds it.

The parked present skill (silent, stamp) as fpl:present:silent and fpl:present:stamp under .agents/skills/, as a child of pull request 191, with per-skill links in .claude/skills/ until S1a's directory link replaces them; a techdebt issue for silent as a pre-push check.

.agents/skills/ as the source of every skill and .claude/skills one symbolic link to it; fpl-conventions removed; CLAUDE.md at most 15 lines; AGENTS.md one screen with the skill tree and planned marks; the two sentences declaring the docs canonical gone; a QUALITY.md paragraph naming the skills-cover gate; these rows. Waits on pull request 192's fpl-run skill moving to .agents/skills/fpl:run.

scripts/gates-list (pull request 195) also discovers .agents/skills/*/scripts/*-self-test and # gates: headers there; skills-cover with its self-test under .agents/skills/fpl:quality:skills/scripts/ (rules SKILLS-UNCOVERED, -RATCHET-STALE, -RATCHET-REASON, -NAME, -LINK, -SUB, -SCREEN; --uncovered prints ratchet lines); quality/skills-ratchet generated; a replay over main and the open pull request tips gives 0 refusals with the ratchet.

fpl:pr:* and fpl:land:*; pr and whoami-check move into the skills' scripts/ (land stays, land.yml names it); pr --ready with derived guards, bots silent and threads resolved; the WORKFLOW.md paragraphs they replace go.

fpl:commit:* and fpl:series:*; boundary, series and restack move (acommit, agent-identity, commit-lint, branch-lint and present-check stay, workflows name them); COMMITS.md keeps the authorship model and loses the procedure.

scripts/present as a state machine with a ledger present/STATE.json, states derived from artefacts (silent, rewritten, stamped, checked, leak-clean, carded, ready), present status and present graph --mermaid; fpl:present with one sub-skill per state; presenter.md shrinks to ten lines; a SKILLS-GRAPH self-test keeps the skill's Mermaid equal to the script's. Waits on pull requests 190 and 191.
fpl:worktree:* and fpl:leak; new-worktree, layer, sweep and leak-check move into the skills' scripts/; every hook call site reaches them through the repository root.

fpl:quality:* and fpl:task:*; crap, props, escapes, mutants, gates, task and rad-cob-dagtaak move (diagrams, wip-count and brake-flip stay, workflows name them); the paths in quality/noslop.mk follow. Waits on pull request 195.
fpl:review:*; review, review-serve, export-review and import-review move into the skill's scripts/; or a ratchet line with the maintainer's reason instead.
